articles.title: US radar facility at Bahrain base attacked with six drones, IRGC claims
articles.summary:
US radar facility at Bahrain base attacked with six drones, IRGC claims

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said their forces carried out a drone attack on a US radar system at a base in Bahrain, according to a statement carried by the Iranian state broadcaster on Sunday. 

"The U.S. air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force," the Guards said in a statement posted by the state broadcaster on Telegram. 

Earlier, Bahrain issued two danger alerts within a span of more than two hours, urging citizens to stay calm and move to safer places.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts third drone as Houthis claim downing aircraft
articles.summary:
Saudi-led coalition intercepts third drone as Houthis claim downing aircraft

Saudi-led coalition forces have shot down yet another Houthi drone in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Region, according to Colonel Turki al-Malki, spokesman for the coalition.

It’s the third drone the coalition says it has shot down over the region in the last three hours, along with two ballistic missiles that were headed for Riyadh.

Meanwhile, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on X that they have shot down a Saudi Arabian armed reconnaissance aircraft in the airspace of al-Jawf.

Saree said this is the fifth aircraft the Houthis have shot down since the escalation began.

articles.title: Trump may not attack Iran as long as it doesn't provoke US, report says
articles.summary:
Trump may not attack Iran as long as it doesn't provoke US, report says

President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent days that he may hold off on attacking Iran if the US faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, according to three people familiar with the matter.

Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the war with new strikes and winding down hostilities, and current and former officials say he does not appear to have made up his mind about how to resolve the unpopular conflict, which he launched in February with Israel.

But in meetings with his national security advisers and after a series of intelligence briefings, Trump said he was considering holding off on strikes, said the people, who, like others interviewed for this story, spoke on condition of anonymity.

He has also indicated sympathy for allies in the region who have asked him not to return to a full-fledged war.

"I could end it immediately, but at the request of the nations that I am looking to protect, we are doing it a little bit longer way, a bit more civilly," Trump told sports broadcaster Stephen A. Smith on Thursday.

Trump's private comments build on public remarks playing down the likelihood of major warfare resuming.

CALLS WITH SAUDI ARABIA AND TURKEY

In phone calls over the past two weeks, Trump asked for opinions from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan, who both urged him not to resume attacks on Iran, according to a senior US official and another person familiar with the matter. They said Trump made no commitment either way.

Trump told bin Salman on 31 October that he was planning to attack after the elections, but the crown prince pleaded for him to hold off, arguing that economic sanctions against Iran were working, according to two more people familiar with the discussion.

Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

Trump has spoken with Erdogan three times since 28 October, according to Turkey's presidency. An official readout from the 7 November call stressed that tensions between Iran and the US need to end.

MILITARY OPTIONS

At the same time, the US military is ready to escalate if needed, three more people familiar with US planning said.

A third aircraft carrier is moving into the Middle East in the coming days to replace one of the two currently operating in the region, but all three carriers could stay if needed, the people said.

Trump could opt to bomb Iran's underground nuclear facilities, one of the people familiar with Trump's calls with the Saudi and Turkish leaders said. But the US has already struck those facilities, and it is unclear whether further strikes would be successful.

ISRAELI PRESSURE

Israeli officials have continued to lobby the administration to engage in another military campaign, according to a US official.

Trump signalled this week that the US has already achieved what it could from negotiations, but did not say whether he would resume strikes.

Report by Reuters

Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, an Iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.
